title: Aion 2 Training tips for aimbot and ESP practice
desc: Training and private-lobby workflows to tune aimbot, ESP wallhack and drop ESP before Abyss PvP.

body.text: Training and private lobbies are training tools—not the same as private aion 2 cheats used in Abyss PvP. Use them to tune [Pro aimbot](/products/aion-2-cheats/) and ESP ranges before going live on NCSOFT.

items: Load the Abyss preset with high smoothness and moderate FOV.
Run staff mid-range skill chains for five minutes without changing sliders.
Switch to bow close-range tracking, then gun finisher timing.
Only lower smoothness after tracking looks human in replays.
Save a Training grounds profile separate from your Abyss preset.
Start player boxes and skeletons at 1200 units max distance.
Enable health bars and distance readouts; turn off portrait spam.
Add drop and drop ESP only after boxes feel natural.
Pair with [ESP wallhack setup](/blog/aion-2-esp-wallhack-setup/) for Abyss PvP translation.
Test stream-proof mode with a 30-second OBS recording.
Keep mini-radar on for gank calls.
Practice rotating on zone with radar dots, not tunnel vision.
Disable cluttered loot timers until zone clears feel clean.
Supports use radar to call rotates; fraggers use it to avoid stacked fights.
See [radar hack guide](/blog/aion-2-radar-hack-guide/) for FOV caps.
Fill a private instance for semi-realistic team fights.
Practice one class profile at a time—staff, then bow, then gun.
Kick extra bots so only the targets you need remain.
Private Training instances are the safest place to test [Skill aim assist guide](/blog/aion-2-skill-script-guide/) before Abyss PvP.
Never first-session a new preset in Abyss PvP on patch day.
